reason: The single cited passage (E1) directly demonstrates phase-selective recrystallization in a eutectic high-entropy alloy, achieving ~35% uniform elongation and ~2 GPa true stress, and explicitly states the mechanism of eliminating weak boundaries to release strain hardening capacity. However, the passage reports true stress rather than yield strength, and the hypothesis adds pre-deformation and annealing details not described in E1, representing a minor overstatement of what the evidence directly supports.
premises: Phase-selective recrystallization of the soft phase in a duplex eutectic alloy is feasible via controlled thermo-mechanical treatment
Such treatment eliminates weak phase boundaries in the soft phase
Eliminating weak boundaries fully releases strain hardening capacity of the duplex phases
The resulting microstructure (recrystallized soft phase in hard-phase skeleton) simultaneously improves strength and ductility over the as-cast state
The concept is applicable to the specific fcc+B2 eutectic high-entropy alloy system proposed
